the-prompt-is-a-safeguard.header: The prompt is a safeguard, not an error
the-prompt-is-a-safeguard.description: A model can be steered by text it reads, such as a web page or a project file, so OWASP recommends requiring a human to approve high-impact actions; each vendor builds that approval into its default mode [1][2][3][4][5][6][7].

codex-approvals.title: OpenAI, Codex: Agent approvals and security

claude-codes-prompt.description: In manual mode, commands outside a built-in read-only set trigger a "Bash command" dialog asking "Do you want to proceed?" with Yes, "Yes, and don't ask again" and No. Prompt names and defaults differ by AI agent and version and change often, so recheck before showing one on screen [1].

why-approvals-are-kept.description: Anthropic says broad file access is risky especially under prompt injection; this is a vendor statement, not an independent study [1].

claude-code-sandboxing.title: Anthropic, Making Claude Code more secure and autonomous with sandboxing

type-the-skill.title: Type the skill
type-the-skill.script: Type the name of the skill, hancrafted-check-setup, and your AI agent reads it. Before it does anything on your computer, it stops and asks you. That pause is not an error, it is the AI agent handing the decision to you.

say-yes.title: Say yes
say-yes.script: You are the one who decides here, so look at what it wants to run. For this skill, it opens one web page, and the answer is yes. If you were ever unsure what a command does, you could ask the AI agent to explain it before you approve. Would you rather have a tool that asks, or one that does not?

the-proof.title: The proof
the-proof.script: Approve it, and the hancrafted homepage opens in your browser. That is the whole check, and there is nothing more to submit. You just ran a skill, so see you at the workshop, and until then, have a look around hancrafted. If the page does not open, the skill prints the link, and you can open it by hand.
